rules: NOTE ON COMPLETENESS: I was cut off after only one 32-case probe batch, so /tmp/spec/refs.md was NOT written and the deliverable is incomplete. Everything below is verified by actual probes of /workspace/dataset/test2_executable; the 'uncertain' list marks what remains unprobed.

Two outcome classes only: (a) instance-validation failure -> stdout = e.message + "\n", rc=0; (b) reference-resolution failure or RecursionError -> stdout = "" (nothing), rc=1, traceback on stderr. There is no third class. So a JS implementer must map every unresolvable-$ref and every unbounded-$ref-cycle to `process.exit(1)` with empty stdout.

$ref resolves against the schema document root for "#/..." JSON Pointer fragments. Both "#/$defs/x" and "#/definitions/x" work under 2020-12 (definitions is just an ordinary object member reachable by pointer, not a recognized keyword).

Pointers may target ANY location, not just $defs: "#/properties/a" resolves to the properties subschema and validates with it. "#/prefixItems/0" likewise. Any JSON value reachable by pointer is usable as a schema.
Multi-level pointers work: "#/$defs/a/$defs/b" -> {"$defs":{"a":{"$defs":{"b":{...}}}}} resolves fine.

POINTER TO NON-EXISTENT LOCATION -> rc=1, stdout="" (NOT a ValidationError, so nothing is printed). Verified for: "#/$defs/nope" (missing key), "#/nope/deep" (missing intermediate), "#/$defs/x/nope" (descending past a leaf).

PERCENT-DECODING HAPPENS ON THE WHOLE FRAGMENT BEFORE SPLITTING ON "/". This is the single biggest trap. Evidence: "#/$defs/a%20b" finds key "a b" (ok); "#/$defs/a%25b" finds key "a%b" (ok); "#/$defs/%C3%A9" finds key "é" (ok, UTF-8 decoding); but "#/$defs/a%2Fb" with key "a/b" FAILS rc=1 -- because %2F decodes to "/" first and then becomes a segment separator, yielding segments ["$defs","a","b"]. A naive implementer who decodes per-segment would wrongly make %2F work.

Raw (undecoded) literals also work where they are valid JSON string content: "#/$defs/a b" (literal space) finds "a b"; "#/$defs/a%b" finds "a%b" (a lone % that is not a valid escape is left alone -- Python unquote behavior); "#/$defs/é" (raw UTF-8) finds "é"; "#/$defs/" finds the empty-string key "".

JSON-Pointer ~ escapes are honored: "~0" -> "~" ("#/$defs/a~0b" finds key "a~b"), "~1" -> "/" ("#/$defs/a~1b" finds key "a/b"). Tilde unescaping happens per-segment AFTER the split, i.e. after percent-decoding.

ARRAY POINTER INDICES USE PYTHON SEMANTICS, NOT JSON-POINTER SEMANTICS. "#/prefixItems/-1" RESOLVES (negative indexing from the end) rather than erroring. "#/prefixItems/5" (out of range) -> rc=1. "#/prefixItems/01" (leading zero) -> rc=1. "#/prefixItems/a" (non-numeric) -> rc=1. A JS implementer must special-case negative integers as `arr.length + n`.

$ref to "#" (the root) is legal and works WHEN THE INSTANCE MAKES PROGRESS: {"type":"object","properties":{"a":{"$ref":"#"}}} against {"a":{"a":1}} prints "1 is not of type 'object'\n" rc=0, and against {"a":{"a":"x"}} prints "'x' is not of type 'object'\n" rc=0.

INFINITE $ref CYCLE WITH NO INSTANCE PROGRESS -> rc=1, stdout="" (Python RecursionError). Verified: {"$ref":"#"} alone -> rc=1; {"$ref":"#","type":"string"} -> rc=1 (the sibling type check never gets a chance to report, because the recursion blows up first); {"$ref":""} -> rc=1 (the empty fragment also resolves to the root, so it self-recurses).
$ref = "" (empty string) is NOT an error-in-resolution -- it resolves to the current document root, and therefore self-recurses to rc=1 in a root-level schema. Do not implement "" as unresolvable.

SIBLING KEYWORDS NEXT TO $ref DO STILL APPLY (2020-12 behavior; $ref does not short-circuit). Verified: {"$ref":"#/$defs/x","type":"string","$defs":{"x":{"minimum":5}}} against 1 -> "1 is less than the minimum of 5
"; {"$ref":"#/$defs/x","$defs":{"x":{"type":"string"}},"minimum":5} against 1 -> "1 is not of type 'string'
"; {"$ref":"#/$defs/x","type":"string","$defs":{"x":{"minLength":5}}} against "ab" -> "'ab' is too short
". In all three probes the $ref-derived error was the one printed and $ref appeared first in JSON key order.

Errors surfacing from inside a $ref'd subschema are INDISTINGUISHABLE from inline errors: the message template is identical and no path/ref prefix is added. {"$ref":"#/$defs/x","$defs":{"x":{"type":"string"}}} against 1 prints exactly "1 is not of type 'string'\n" -- the same text as a bare {"type":"string"}. e.message never mentions the ref, the pointer, or the schema path.

The single printed message is selected by jsonschema's best_match over iter_errors, not simply the first error. Its relevance key is (-len(instance_path), instance_path, validator not in {anyOf,oneOf}, validator in {}, not is_type(instance,'object')), resolved by Python min() which keeps the FIRST minimum, so equal-relevance sibling errors fall back to schema key insertion order. For refs specifically: a $ref-derived error and a sibling-keyword error at the same instance path tie on every component and thus resolve by JSON key order. This is inferred from the observed $ref-wins-when-first probes and needs the type-before-$ref probe to confirm.
$defs / definitions are not themselves validated as schemas at instance time; only the parts actually reached via $ref are used. A $defs entry that is garbage is harmless unless referenced.
surprises: Percent-decoding is applied to the ENTIRE fragment before splitting on "/", so "%2F" becomes a real path separator and CANNOT be used to escape a slash inside a key. "#/$defs/a%2Fb" fails (rc=1) even though $defs has the key "a/b"; you must write "#/$defs/a~1b" instead. Naive per-segment decoding gets this backwards.

Array indices in pointers follow Python list indexing, so "#/prefixItems/-1" successfully resolves to the LAST element instead of raising. JSON Pointer forbids this. Meanwhile "#/prefixItems/01" (leading zero) is rejected, matching JSON Pointer.
A lone "%" that is not a valid percent-escape is passed through unchanged rather than erroring: "#/$defs/a%b" resolves key "a%b".
An unresolvable $ref prints NOTHING and exits 1 -- it is not a ValidationError. Implementers who emit a friendly "unresolvable reference" message on stdout will mismatch on every such case.

$ref:"" (empty string) resolves to the document root, which means a root-level {"$ref":""} is an infinite self-recursion (rc=1), not a resolution failure. Same rc, different reason, so it happens to be safe -- but the reasoning matters for nested cases.

A self-recursive $ref only survives if the instance shrinks; {"$ref":"#"} with no instance progress is a hard rc=1 RecursionError, and a sibling keyword that WOULD have produced a clean ValidationError ({"$ref":"#","type":"string"}) is still lost to the recursion -- so recursion detection must happen before/independently of sibling evaluation.
"definitions" works under 2020-12 not because the keyword is recognized but because a JSON Pointer can address any member; so "#/definitions/x" and "#/anythingElse/x" behave the same.
uncertain: DELIVERABLE NOT WRITTEN: /tmp/spec/refs.md does not exist. I completed only 1 of ~8 planned probe batches (32 of the required 60+ cases) before being told to finalize. The spec file must still be authored.

ENTIRELY UNPROBED: external/absolute $ref ("https://example.com/s.json") -- whether a network fetch is attempted, rc, stdout, and wall-clock time/timeout. Also unprobed: "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" (possibly bundled) and $ref to the 2020-12 metaschema URI.
ENTIRELY UNPROBED: $id base-URI changes, relative $ref resolution against an $id, $ref to a sibling $id'd subschema, $id inside $defs, and $id with a trailing empty fragment.
ENTIRELY UNPROBED: $anchor and "#name" plain-name fragment refs; anchor name validity rules; anchor vs pointer fragment disambiguation; duplicate anchors.
ENTIRELY UNPROBED: $dynamicRef / $dynamicAnchor recursive-extension behavior, and whether the 2019-09 spellings $recursiveRef / $recursiveAnchor are ignored or honored under the 2020-12 dialect.

ENTIRELY UNPROBED: the whole $schema sub-task -- which dialect URIs are recognized (draft-03/04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12), with and without trailing "#", http vs https; whether an UNKNOWN $schema URI errors and with what rc; and per-dialect behavior differences (items-as-array, exclusiveMinimum:true, dependencies, $defs vs definitions). I cannot say which dialects the JS implementer must support.

The exact exception types behind rc=1 are unconfirmed -- stderr was truncated by the harness to the PyInstaller banner line, so I never saw the Python exception class for unresolvable pointers (likely referencing.exceptions.Unresolvable / PointerToNowhere) vs RecursionError. This does not affect stdout/rc matching but would confirm the two failure paths are distinct.

Whether the tilde-unescape and percent-decode ordering claim is fully right: I confirmed decode-then-split, but did not probe the discriminating cases "~01" (should give "~1") or "%7E0" (would give "~" if decoded before unescaping).

Whether a sibling keyword listed BEFORE $ref in JSON key order wins the best_match tie ({"type":"string","$ref":"..."}). All my sibling probes had $ref first, so the key-insertion-order rule is inferred, not demonstrated.

Negative-index behavior was probed only on a 1-element array, where [-1] and [0] coincide. Needs a 2+-element array to prove true Python negative indexing (and to test -3 on a 2-element array, presumably rc=1).

rules: PROG: hardcode the literal string `test2_executable` (argparse uses basename(argv[0]); proven via symlink). Do NOT derive from process.argv — that would give `test2.mjs`. It appears in the `usage:` line and the `<prog>: error:` line.

EXIT CODES: 0 = "valid\n" | ValidationError message+"\n" | help text. 1 = json.loads failure / SchemaError (stdout EMPTY, traceback on stderr). 2 = any argparse error (stdout EMPTY, usage+error on stderr).

HELP goes to STDOUT and exits 0. Exact default text: `usage: test2_executable [-h] --a A --b B

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --a A       instance data (JSON string)
  --b B       schema (JSON string)
`. Header is `options:` (not `optional arguments:`); help column starts at char 14; one blank line after usage; no trailing blank line.
-h and --help are byte-identical. Abbreviations --h / --he / --hel also print help. --a and --b have no abbreviations; --ab, --a1, --A, ---a, -a, -b are all UNKNOWN options.

ERROR FORMAT (rc 2, stderr): `<usage block>\n test2_executable: error: <msg>\n`. The error line is NEVER wrapped regardless of COLUMNS. Only 5 messages exist: E1 `the following arguments are required: --a` / `--b` / `--a, --b`; E2 `argument --a: expected one argument`; E3 `unrecognized arguments: <argv tokens joined by single space, argv order, no quoting>`; E4 `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '<rest>'`; E5 `ambiguous option: <tok> could match --help, --a, --b`.
PRECEDENCE (strict): E5 (pre-scan) > E2/E4 (consume pass, earliest offending token) > help(rc 0) > E1 required > E3 unrecognized > json.loads(--a) > json.loads(--b) > validate.

Help beats E1 and E3 even when the help flag is LAST: ["--nonsense","-h"], ["--a","1","--b","true","zzz","--help"] all print help rc 0. But help LOSES to an E2/E4 raised at an earlier argv index, and always loses to E5.
REPEATED options: LAST occurrence wins (plain store), mixing = and space forms doesn't matter. A discarded earlier value is NEVER JSON-parsed: ["--a","{bad","--b","true","--a","1"] -> "valid\n" rc 0.
REQUIRED check runs BEFORE the unrecognized check: ["--","--a","1","--b","true"] -> E1 `required: --a, --b`, not E3.

VALUE-vs-OPTION classification for a token in an option's value slot. Accepted as a value iff: (a) it is "", (b) it does not start with '-', (c) it is exactly "-", (d) it matches /^-\d+$|^-\d*\.\d+$/, or (e) it contains an ASCII space 0x20 ANYWHERE. Otherwise it is option-like and triggers E2.
Negative-number regex has NO exponent branch: -5, -5.5, -0.5, -.5, -12345678901234567890 are values; -1e5, -5x, --5 are option-like (E2).
Rule (e) is ASCII 0x20 ONLY: "-5 ", "- 5", "-x y", "--b c" are VALUES; "-5\t", "-\t5", "-\n5", and "- 5" (NBSP) are option-like -> E2.

`--` is NOT a no-op and is NOT consumed (no positionals exist). It (1) stops the ambiguity pre-scan, (2) makes every later token a plain positional, (3) itself lands in extras. ["--a","1","--b","true","--"] -> E3 `unrecognized arguments: --`. ["--a","--","1"] -> E2 (`--` blocks value lookahead).
`--a=VALUE` works; `--a=` gives the empty string -> json.loads("") -> rc 1, stdout empty. `--a=--b`, `--a=-5`, `--a= 1` all pass the raw text through.

-h + TAIL family: -hx, -hxyz, -h1, -hx=1, -hé, -help all PRINT HELP rc 0 (help action is queued, then the unresolved short flag is silently dropped into extras). But -h-, -h--, -h-x -> E4 with '-'/'--'/'-x'; and -h=1, --help=1, --h=1, --he=x -> E4 with the text after '='. -xh is just an unknown option (no decomposition).

E5 (ambiguous) is reachable ONLY via `--=<anything>`: --=1, --=, --=x=y. It fires in a left-to-right PRE-SCAN over all argv before `--`, so it beats even a leading -h. ---=1 and -=1 are ordinary unknown options.
E5 match-list order is dict insertion order: `--help, --a, --b` (--help FIRST because add_help runs before the two add_argument calls). Not alphabetical.
E1 name order is declaration order: `--a, --b`, joined with ", ".
E3 joins extras with a single space and no quoting: [""] -> `unrecognized arguments: ` (trailing space); ["",""] -> `unrecognized arguments:  ` (two spaces). Tabs/newlines emitted literally.
No fromfile_prefix_chars: `@file` is a literal token, never expanded.
No positional arguments are defined, so any bare token becomes an extra (E3) preserving argv order: ["x","--a","1","y","--b","true","z"] -> `unrecognized arguments: x y z`.
--a is json.loads'ed BEFORE --b (source lines 11 then 12). If both are invalid, the --a failure is the one raised. Both give rc 1 with empty stdout.

HELP/USAGE WIDTH: width = COLUMNS-2, where COLUMNS is parsed with Python int() semantics (whitespace-stripped, optional sign, underscores between digits, Unicode Nd digits; "12abc"/"30.0"/"0x1e"/"_30" invalid); invalid or <=0 falls back to tty width, else 80. LINES has no effect.

COLUMNS >= 47 (width >= 45) yields output byte-identical to the default; COLUMNS=46 already differs. Hardcoding the 80-col string is safe only if the grader never sets a narrow COLUMNS or a narrow tty.

Usage wrapping tokens are ['[-h]','--a','A','--b','B'] (argparse splits on \S+, so `--a` and `A` can land on different lines). Three usage layouts by text_width w: w>=40 single line; 31<=w<=39 continuation indent 24 spaces; w<=30 prog on line 1 then 7-space indent. Full greedy-fill algorithm in spec §4.3.

Options-section geometry: max_help_position = min(24, max(width-20, 4)); help_position = min(14, max_help_position); help_width = max(width-help_position, 11); action_width = help_position-4. Header inline if len(header) <= action_width (padEnd to action_width + 2 spaces), else header alone on its own line with help indented help_position. Validated for COLUMNS 1..140.
Node: use process.argv.slice(2). Node passes every token after the script path through untouched, including --help, -h, --, --inspect, -e, --print.

Invalid-UTF-8 argv bytes: Python surrogateescape maps byte 0xNN to U+DCNN and repr() renders it as the 6 ASCII chars \udcNN, so stdout stays ASCII and rc is 0 (e.g. --a $'"\xff"' --b '{"type":"number"}' -> `'\udcff' is not of type 'number'\n`). Node's process.argv lossily maps these to U+FFFD; recover raw bytes from /proc/self/cmdline if this matters.
Large payloads are fine (50k-element array -> 150013 bytes on stdout, rc 0); flush stdout before process.exit() to avoid truncation.
A validated runnable model of all of the above is at /tmp/spec/argparse_ref.mjs (0 mismatches vs the binary over 1706 argv vectors and 1595 width×argv combos).
surprises: `-hx` / `-hxyz` / `-help` / `-hé` PRINT HELP with rc 0 — a naive implementer errors on the unknown tail. The help action is queued first, the unresolved `-x` is silently discarded into extras, then the queued help runs and exits 0. Yet `-h-x` and `-h=1` DO error (E4).
`-hx=1` prints help but `-h=1` errors — because the short-prefix rule resolves `-h`+tail `x` before the `=` rule is ever consulted.
The `--=1` ambiguity error fires in a PRE-SCAN and beats everything, including a `-h` that appears earlier in argv. But `["--","--=1"]` does not error ambiguously, because the pre-scan stops at `--`.
`--` is not swallowed: with no positional actions defined, a trailing `--` shows up verbatim in `unrecognized arguments: --`.
Missing-required (E1) is checked BEFORE unrecognized (E3), so `["--","--a","1","--b","true"]` reports missing --a/--b rather than the 5 leftover tokens.
`--a -5` works (negative numbers are accepted as values because no option looks like a negative number) but `--a -1e5` fails with `expected one argument` — the regex has no exponent branch.

A leading-dash token containing an ASCII space is accepted as a value (`--a "-x y"` works), but a tab or newline or U+00A0 does not trigger this — only 0x20. This is very easy to get wrong, and NBSP renders identically to a space in most debug output.
Repeated options silently take the LAST value and the earlier value is never JSON-parsed, so `--a '{bad' --b true --a 1` prints `valid` instead of failing.
The help output is terminal-width dependent (COLUMNS or tty), and `max_help_position` is itself width-dependent: min(24, max(width-20, 4)). Narrow widths change indentation, not just wrapping.
In the usage line, `--a` and `A` are independent wrap tokens, so a narrow terminal can produce `usage: test2_executable [-h] --a A --b` / `                        B`.
The ambiguous-option match list is `--help, --a, --b` — `--help` first, because add_help() runs before the add_argument calls. Neither alphabetical nor declaration order of the user's arguments.
Help is printed to STDOUT with exit code 0, whereas every argparse error goes entirely to STDERR with exit code 2 and completely empty stdout.
Invalid UTF-8 in argv does NOT crash: the bytes become surrogates and repr() escapes them to plain ASCII `\udcNN` in the stdout message, rc 0.
uncertain: Whether the grader sets COLUMNS or attaches a tty. If neither (normal piped harness), the hardcoded 80-column help string is exact; the full width formula in §4.3 covers every other case. Risk window is only COLUMNS <= 46.
Exact prog if argv[0] were empty or had a trailing slash — unreachable normally and irrelevant since the JS port must hardcode `test2_executable`.

Full surrogateescape fidelity in JS. I confirmed the Python mapping (byte 0xNN -> U+DCNN -> ASCII text `\udcNN`) and that /proc/self/cmdline preserves raw bytes, but did not build a JS decoder nor probe every malformed-UTF-8 shape (overlong encodings, truncated 4-byte sequences, 0xF5-0xFF mid-sequence).
Behaviour when stdout is closed / EPIPE (Python BrokenPipeError vs Node default) — not probed, assumed out of scope.

The exact Python/argparse patch version. Behaviour matches a 3.12-era argparse. If the binary is ever rebuilt on a different Python, the `-h`+tail rules (§6.7) and the width-dependent max_help_position (§4.3) are the two likeliest places to drift.
Whether any ambiguous-option trigger other than `--=<anything>` exists. I probed --=1, --=, --=x=y, ---=1, -=1 and found none, but did not exhaustively enumerate all `--`-prefixed strings.
OS argv length limits (tested up to ~300 KB per argument, which worked).
